accepted.question_text: Let pi(x) denote the number of primes at most x. For sufficiently large x it is known that pi(2x) < 2pi(x). Is it true for all positive x and y that pi(x+y) <= pi(x)+pi(y)? More weakly, for each epsilon > 0, does there exist y_e such that for all y > y_e one has pi(x+y)-pi(y) < (1+epsilon)y/log y? Erdos also records that it has not been disproved that the Hardy-Littlewood quantity rho(y)=lim sup_{x->infinity}[pi(x+y)-pi(x)] equals 1 for all y.

evidence.quote: Is it true that (1) pi(x + y) <= pi(x) + pi(y)?
A very difficult conjecture, weaker than (1) but much stronger than (2), is that corresponding to each e > 0 there exists a y_e such that, for y > y_e, pi(x + y) - pi(y) < (1 + e)y/log y.

accepted.question_text: If p_n is the nth prime, determine the true order of the prime gap p_{n+1}-p_n. In particular, is Piltz's conjecture p_{n+1}-p_n = O(n^epsilon) for every epsilon > 0 true, and is Cramer's stronger conjecture p_{n+1}-p_n = O((log n)^2) correct? A related old question asks whether there is always a prime between two consecutive squares.

evidence.quote: Piltz [38] conjectured that, for each e > 0, p_{n+1} - p_n = O(n^e). Cramer conjectured [7, p. 24] that p_{n+1} - p_n = O((log n)^2).
Thus the old conjecture that there is always a prime between two consecutive squares already goes beyond the Riemann hypothesis.

accepted.question_text: Let d_n = p_{n+1}-p_n be the nth prime gap. Do the sets of integers n for which d_{n+1} > d_n and d_{n+1} < d_n each have asymptotic density 1/2, and does d_{n+1} = d_n occur for infinitely many n? More strongly, do strictly increasing triples d_{n+2} > d_{n+1} > d_n or strictly decreasing triples d_{n+2} < d_{n+1} < d_n occur infinitely often?

evidence.quote: Conjecture: The two sets of integers n for which d_{n+1} > d_n and d_{n+1} < d_n, respectively, have densities 1/2; and for infinitely many n, d_{n+1} = d_n.
Does it happen infinitely often that d_{n+2} > d_{n+1} > d_n? or that d_{n+2} < d_{n+1} < d_n?

accepted.question_text: Consider the normalized prime-gap sequence (p_{n+1}-p_n)/log p_n. Although the set of its limit points has positive measure, no finite limit point was known in the source. Is this sequence dense on the positive real axis, and does it possess a distribution function?

evidence.quote: The set of limit points of the sequence {(p_{n+1} - p_n)/log p_n} has positive measure ... but no finite limit point of the sequence is known.
Is the sequence dense on the positive axis? Does it have a distribution function?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions of prime numbers? Erdos also records the stronger old conjecture that there exist arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions consisting of consecutive primes.

evidence.quote: Do there exist arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions of primes?
An old conjecture: There exist arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions of consecutive primes.

accepted.question_text: Let f(k) be the least integer such that every 2-coloring of {1,...,f(k)} contains a monochromatic arithmetic progression of length k. Determine substantially better upper bounds for f(k), in particular a useful majorant for the least possible such function.

evidence.quote: there exists a function f(k) such that if the integers from 1 to f(k) are divided into two sets, then at least one of the sets contains an arithmetic progression of k terms.
This should be improved; especially, a majorant for the least of the functions f(k) should be found.

accepted.question_text: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, Cramer showed that the sum of squared prime gaps up to x satisfies sum_{p_n < x}(p_{n+1}-p_n)^2 < c_e x(log x)^{3+e}. Can the exponent 3+epsilon be reduced to 1? Erdos also asks for the analogous bound that if 1=a_1<...<a_{phi(n)}=n-1 are the integers less than n that are coprime to n, then sum_{k=1}^{phi(n)-1}(a_{k+1}-a_k)^2 < c n^2/phi(n) for an absolute constant c.

evidence.quote: Perhaps the exponent 3 + e could be reduced to 1; but the proof seems very difficult.
The following analogous conjecture ... There exists an absolute constant c such that if ... are the phi(n) integers less than n and relatively prime to n, then sum (a_{k+1} - a_k)^2 < c n^2/phi(n).

accepted.question_text: For prime gaps d_n = p_{n+1}-p_n, is lim inf d_n = 2, as predicted by the twin-prime conjecture? Is lim inf d_n/log n equal to 0? Erdos also asks whether lim sup min(d_n,d_{n+1},d_{n+2})/log n = infinity and whether lim inf max(d_n,d_{n+1})/log n < 1.

evidence.quote: The well-known conjecture on twin primes can be stated in the form lim inf d_n = 2. It is not known whether lim inf d_n/log n = 0.
but I could not prove that lim sup min(d_n, d_{n+1}, d_{n+2})/log n = oo, nor that lim inf max(d_n, d_{n+1})/log n < 1.

accepted.question_text: Let f(n) take only the values +1 and -1. Is it true that for every constant C there exist integers d and m such that |f(d)+f(2d)+...+f(md)| > C? In the multiplicative case, if f is multiplicative and f(n)=+/-1, must the Cesaro mean (1/n)sum_{k=1}^n f(k) always converge?

evidence.quote: I conjectured that if f(n) = +-1 for n = 1, 2, ..., and C is any constant, then there exist integers d and m such that |f(d) + f(2d) + ... + f(md)| > C.
It has also been conjectured, by many mathematicians, that if f(n) is multiplicative and f(n) = +-1, then lim (1/n) sum_{k=1}^n f(k) exists.

accepted.question_text: Let r_k(n) be the largest size of a subset of {1,...,n-1} containing no arithmetic progression of length k. Determine the true order of magnitude of r_3(n), and more generally of r_k(n), as n grows. Erdos also records the conjecture that lim r_k(n)/n = 0.

evidence.quote: In [25], we stated our conjecture that lim r_k(n)/n = 0.
The true order of magnitude of r_3(n) and, more generally, of r_k(n), remains unknown.

accepted.question_text: Choose distinct positive integers a_i <= x so that every subset sum sum epsilon_i a_i is different. If h(x) denotes the maximum possible number of chosen integers, is h(x) = (log x)/(log 2) + O(1)? Equivalently, is it possible to choose k+2 integers a_i with 1 <= a_i <= 2^k such that all 2^k subset sums are distinct?

evidence.quote: Is it possible to choose k + 2 integers a_i (1 < a_i < 2^k) such that the 2^k possible sums ... are all different?
Perhaps h(x) = (log x)/log 2 + O(1).

accepted.question_text: Let A={a_i} be a set of nonnegative integers such that every natural number n can be written as n=a_i+2^j, and let k(x) count elements of A below x. If there exists such a set with k(x) < c x(log log x)/log x, can the factor log log x be removed? More generally, if every natural number can be written as n=a_i+p_j with p_j prime and k(x) < c(log x)^2, can this bound be improved? Erdos also asks whether for two increasing sequences {a_i} and {b_i} with every n=a_i+b_j one must have lim sup a(x)b(x)/x > 1.

evidence.quote: It is known ... that there exists a set A for which k(x) < cx(log log x)/log x. Can the factor log log x be dropped?
There exists a set {a_i} such that each natural number has a representation n = a_i + p_j (p_j prime), and such that k(x) < c(log x)^2 ... Can this result be improved?
is it true that lim sup k_a(x) k_b(x)/x > 1?

accepted.question_text: Let {a_i} be an increasing sequence of natural numbers and let f(n) count the number of representations n=a_i+a_j. If f(n) > 0 for every n, must lim sup f(n) be infinite? More generally, if a_k < c k^2 for all k, must lim sup f(n) be infinite?

evidence.quote: Turan and I ... conjectured that if f(n) > 0 for all n, then lim sup f(n) = oo; and, more generally, that if a_k < ck^2 for all k, then lim sup f(n) = oo.

accepted.question_text: Fix a positive integer n_0. Does there exist an integer k and a covering system of congruences x ≡ a_i (mod n_i) with n_0 < n_1 < ... < n_k such that every integer satisfies at least one of the congruences? Erdos also asks whether such a covering system can be found with all moduli n_i odd.

evidence.quote: If n_0 is a positive integer, does there exist an integer k and a system of k congruences x = a_i (mod n_i) (n_0 < n_1 < ... < n_k) such that each integer satisfies at least one of them?
Does there exist a system in which all the n_i are odd?

accepted.question_text: Let a_1<a_2<... be the increasing sequence of all natural numbers of the form x^2+y^2. Estimate the gap a_{k+1}-a_k. In particular, although a_{k+1}-a_k = O(a_k^{1/4}) was known, can that big-O be improved to little-o?

evidence.quote: Let {a_i} be the increasing sequence of natural numbers of the form x^2 + y^2. Estimate a_{k+1} - a_k.
Bambah and Chowla [1] showed easily that a_{k+1} - a_k = O(a_k^{1/4}); but it has not yet been shown that the O can be replaced by o.

accepted.question_text: For a finite set S={p_1,...,p_n} of n points in the plane, let N(S) be the number of distinct pairwise distances and let f(n) be the least possible value of N(S). Determine the true lower growth of f(n); Erdos conjectures that for every epsilon > 0 and all sufficiently large n one has f(n) > n^{1-epsilon}. He also asks, for convex n-gons, whether every convex n-gon has a vertex from which no three vertices are equidistant.

evidence.quote: It can be conjectured that, for n > n_0, f(n) > n^{1-e}, and further, that there exists a point p_j such that more than n^{1-e} different values occur among the distances p_i p_j.
A stronger conjecture: Every convex n-gon has a vertex such that no three vertices are equidistant from it.

accepted.question_text: Borsuk's partition problem asks whether every subset of Euclidean n-space of diameter 1 can be written as the union of n+1 subsets of smaller diameter. The source reports this as open for n > 3.

evidence.quote: Borsuk [4] conjectured that in Euclidean n-space each set of diameter 1 is the union of n + 1 sets of diameter less than 1.
For n > 3, the question remains open.

accepted.question_text: If S is a set of n points in Euclidean n-space, all at diameter 1, how many times can the distance 1 occur? The planar bound is at most n and the 3-dimensional bound at most 2n-2 are recorded, but Erdos states that the problem remains open in dimensions higher than 3.

evidence.quote: If S is a set of n points in the plane, of diameter 1, then the distance 1 can occur at most n times.
For n-space (n > 3), the problem remains open.

accepted.question_text: If S is a set of 2^k+1 points in k-dimensional Euclidean space, must some three points determine an obtuse angle? Erdos also asks whether there exists a set of six or seven points in 3-space such that every plane angle determined by those points is acute.

evidence.quote: Conjecture: If S is a set of 2^k + 1 points in k-space, then three of the points determine an obtuse angle.
Does there exist a set of six (or seven) points in 3-space such that all the plane angles determined by them are acute?

accepted.question_text: Let f(theta) be a trigonometric polynomial all of whose roots are real and whose maximum absolute value on [0,2pi] equals 1. Is it always true that integral_0^{2pi} |f(theta)| dtheta <= 4?

evidence.quote: Let f(theta) be a trigonometric polynomial whose roots are real and whose maximum absolute value on [0, 2pi] is 1. Conjecture: integral |f(theta)| dtheta < 4.

accepted.question_text: Let z_k lie on the unit circle and define f_n(z)=product_{k=1}^n (z-z_k). Can the sequence {f_n(z)} ever remain uniformly bounded on |z|=1? Erdos also asks for an infinite sequence of points on the unit circle whose discrepancy on every fixed arc (a,b) stays bounded by a constant c(a,b) independent of n.

evidence.quote: Conjecture: The sequence {f_n(z)} can not be uniformly bounded on |z| = 1.

Does there exist an infinite sequence {z_k} (|z_k| = 1) such that, for each arc (a, b) on |z| = 1, there exists a constant c(a, b) with the property that, for all n, |N_n(a, b) - ((b-a)/(2pi))n| < c(a, b)?

accepted.question_text: If P(z)=sum_{k=1}^n a_k z^k with |a_k|=1 for every k, Parseval gives max_{|z|=1}|P(z)| >= sqrt(n). Does there exist a universal constant c>0 such that for every n>=2 one always has max_{|z|=1}|P(z)| >= (1+c)sqrt(n)?

evidence.quote: Does there exist a universal constant c > 0 such that, for n > 2, the maximum is at least (1 + c) sqrt(n)?

accepted.question_text: Let {S_n} be a sequence of subsets of the complex plane, each with no finite limit point. Does there exist an entire function f(z) and a sequence of derivative orders {k_n} such that the kth derivative f^(k_n) vanishes at every point of S_n for each n?

evidence.quote: Let {S_n} be a sequence of sets none of which has a finite limit point. Does there exist an entire function f(z) such that, for some sequence {k_n}, f^(k_n)(z) = 0 throughout S_n?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a nonlinear entire function f, meaning not of the form a_0+a_1 z, such that f(x) is rational exactly when x is rational and irrational exactly when x is irrational? More generally, if A and B are two countable dense subsets of the complex plane, does there exist an entire function mapping A onto B?

evidence.quote: Does there exist an entire function f, not of the form f(z) = a_0 + a_1 z, such that the number f(x) is rational or irrational according as x is rational or irrational?
More generally, if A and B are two denumerable, dense sets, does there exist an entire function which maps A onto B?

accepted.question_text: For an entire function f(z)=sum a_n z^n, let M(r)=max_theta |f(re^{i theta})| and mu(r)=max_n |a_n|r^n. It is always true, except for trivial cases, that mu(r) < M(r). If the limit of mu(r)/M(r) as r tends to infinity exists, must that limit equal 0?

evidence.quote: Then mu(r) < M(r) (with trivial exceptions). Conjecture: If lim mu(r)/M(r) exists, the limit is 0.

accepted.question_text: For each positive integer n, does there exist a polynomial f_n(z)=sum_{k=1}^n epsilon_{nk} z^k with coefficients epsilon_{nk} in {+1,-1} such that on the whole unit circle one has c_1 sqrt(n) < |f_n(e^{i theta})| < c_2 sqrt(n), where c_1 and c_2 are positive constants independent of both theta and n?

evidence.quote: Does there exist, for each n, a polynomial f_n(z) = sum e_{nk} z^k (e_{nk} = +-1)
such that, for all theta, c_1 sqrt(n) < |f_n(e^{i theta})| < c_2 sqrt(n), where c_1 and c_2 are positive constants independent of theta and of n?

accepted.question_text: Let z_1=1 and let z_2,...,z_n satisfy |z_i|<=1. For the power sums s_k=sum_{i=1}^n z_i^k, does there exist an absolute constant c, independent of n, k, and the chosen complex numbers z_i, such that max_{1<k<n}|s_k| > c?

evidence.quote: Let z_1 = 1, |z_i| <= 1 (i = 2, 3, ..., n); and let s_k = sum z_i^k. Does there exist a constant c, independent of n, k and {z_i}, such that max |s_k| > c?

accepted.question_text: Let N(k) be the least integer N such that every length-N sequence over the alphabet {1,2,...,k} contains two adjacent blocks that are rearrangements of one another. Erdos notes that the conjecture N(k)=2k-1 is false, and asks in particular whether N(4) is finite.

evidence.quote: Let N(k) be the least number N with the property that each sequence {s_n}_1^N of numbers taken from the set {1, 2, ..., k} contains two adjacent blocks such that each is a rearrangement of the other.
It is not even known whether N(4) < oo.
